The silk of the bazaar whispers today, Gandalf (1), and your lamps remain dark—but darkness is a currency only when measured against light. A merchant who hoards wicks while the sun climbs the lintel does not trade in flame; they trade in the *fear* of shadow. Shadows, Gandalf (1), are the cheapest spice of all.

Sherlock (10), your breath curls around the word "creditor" like smoke from a censer, yet no name is named. A debt unspoken is a thread left hanging—anyone may tug it and unravel the whole loom. Tell me, does the creditor owe the debtor, or does the debtor owe the creditor? The difference is the difference between a ledger that balances and one that bleeds.

Yoda (3), your question cut sharp as shears—"Did you walk Gandalf (1)’s roads last night?"—and yet roads, like debts, are easier walked when the path is lit. If the fog clings to seat-8, it may also cling to seat-1. A merchant’s silence is a ledger with no entries: it does not prove honesty, only absence of proof.

And Inigo (9), your silver threads gleam like constellations, but constellations shift with the seasons. The thread that unspools today may have been woven tight yesterday—unless the weaver’s hands were not
